newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end more than one percent lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end more than one percent lower.

text.p: Swiss shares ended more than one percent lower on Friday, extending the correction which started on Thursday after a string of record highs, dealers said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index was down 1.43 percent or 83.9 points at 5,801.5. The all-share Swiss Performance Index dipped 1.08 percent or 39.83 points at 3,661.1.

The Swiss market has outperformed other exchanges of late, so the effect of a correction might be stronger as well, one dealer said. Earlier this week the SMI rose above the level of 6,000 points for the first time.
Trading should remain volatile before options expiry next Friday, traders said.
Winterthur, Swiss Re and UBS stood at the centre of attention. Financier Martin Ebner's BZ group said it had boosted its Winterthur stake to 18.3 percent in June.
BZ Bank costumers held another five percent, Ebner told reporters, also letting slip that Swiss Reinsurance had built up a five percent stake in Winterthur, which Swiss Re later confirmed.
The news of Swiss Re's stake emerged in a bizarre twist when Winterthur mistakenly told Ebner of it in a letter that Ebner showed to journalists, sparking fresh takeover speculation.
Winterthur shares touched a high of 1,474 francs before dropping to end down 20 at 1,418 francs.
Dealers were unsure about Ebner's intentions. Some saw his stake in Winterthur as an investment. Others believed he may be acting for a third party.
Swiss Re also lost ground and tumbled 67 francs to 2,138.
UBS bearer shares lost 39 francs to 1,685. Ebner said his group had sold all of its UBS bearer shares and had boosted its stake to 25 percent of registered shares from 9.0 percent.
Volume leader Novartis dropped 32 francs to 2,371.
